reviewer: Grok (Mini, 2026-09-18): clause-by-clause vs locked PG 10 / Khazarzar Cesti book 7 Greek; earlier lemma-led scaffold discarded

scope_review.notes: Tip scope is Cesti book 7 pinax + proem + On arming only. Author Sextus Julius Africanus, PG 10 Cesti fragmenta via Khazarzar. Not the letters (those have ANF). Not the whole Cesti. No Scripture quotations in this slice. Pinax blank numeral before horse-taming listed as item 6 by sequence. On arming lock slice ends at the Macedonian successors; remainder stays held until translated.

reviews.notes: Pinax: Τάδε ἔνεστιν ἐν τῷ ζʹ τῶν Ἀφρικανοῦ Κεστῶν rendered as contents of book 7. Blank numeral before Ἵππου τιθασία treated as item 6 by order. Twenty heads: ὁπλίσεως arming; πολεμίων φθορᾶς destruction of enemies; Ἀγωνιστικόν athletic contest (not generic combat); τομὴν πληγέντος cutting of one struck; σιδήρου iron wound; τιθασία taming; μὴ χρεμετίσαι not neigh; ὑπόχυσιν cataract; μὴ πτοεῖσθαι not startled; τάχους speed; Ταράξιππον horse-frightener; ὑποζυγίων pack-animals (not axle); ἡμίονον λακτίζουσαν kicking mule; Θήρα στρατιωτική military hunting; ποταμοῦ πλάτος / τείχους ὕψος river breadth and wall height; Ἤχου κλοπή theft of sound; Ἀγρυπνητικόν staying-awake; ἐλεφάντων elephants; Γεωργίας παράδοξα farming paradoxes; Ἐπισφράγισμα περὶ βέλους seal concerning the missile. Negation kept on 7 and 9 (μὴ). No Scripture.

Proem: Κατὰ λόγον ἢ νόμον ἢ εἱμαρμένην ἢ τύχην — reason / law / fate / chance (four-way kept). ἐκβάσεις, ἐπιγοναὶ καὶ φθοραί, ἀλλοιώσεις καὶ ἰάματα — issues, births and destructions, alterations and healings. καλὸν εἰδέναι kept as it is good to know. ὠφέλειαν ποικίλην — varied profit; θεραπείαν παθῶν / ἱστορίαν ἀπόρρητον / λόγου κάλλος. ἔν τε τοῖς φθάνουσι καὶ τοῖς ἑπομένοις — in what has gone before and in what follows. κατὰ τὸ ἐμαυτοῦ μέτριον κατώρθωται — according to my modest measure it has been achieved (first-person agency kept). No Scripture.

On arming. Καλὸν δὲ ἐν πᾶσι καὶ πόλεμον εἰδέναι. Wonder at differing turn of armed contests: Greeks of Romans, Persians of Greeks, Persians not yet beaten by Romans (μηδέπω kept). Cause: not stratagem-greed nor bulk strength (πλήθους...λόγος οὐδὲ εἷς negation kept) but weapons and war-dress. Heavy panoply: double πῖλος, scale θώραξ, hollow bronze shield two grips, greaves, javelin, close spear equal to royal horse, broad short sword. Run rare, sharp, to get inside missiles. Lock-shields and each fights alone — virtue double. March rests so eagerness not blunted; then speed under the fall of missiles; missile power is length, near-at-hand panoply is safety. Layered helmet vs sling; face and neck free. Spears vs lance-horsemen; opener phalanx; peltasts and slingers behind the wall of arms; short swords for ease and violence. Macedonian successors altered few. No Scripture in this slice.
